Working notes:
- Routing depends mainly on request type; sender, subject phrases (“client asking twice,” “second attempt,” etc.), and region/size are not reliable alone.
- Refunds: option C (regional office) was rejected in every case tested (south/north/east, small/large). B was rejected for a large north refund. Therefore use A (standard queue) for refunds unless contradicted.
- Claims: C (regional office) was accepted for a small north claim (REQ-2406). Route claims to C.
- Invoices: C was rejected for east invoices, both small and large. For a small east invoice (REQ-2400), option D was accepted. If D is available, use D for small east invoices. Do not use C for east invoices. Large east invoice routing remains unresolved; avoid C.
- Accepted patterns seen: small east invoice -> D; small north claim -> C.
- Rejected patterns seen: refunds -> C; large north refund -> B; east invoices -> C.
- Keep testing A for refunds if no better option; use C for claims; use D for small east invoices when offered.
